_readme: The NIST CCVS85 conformance ledger. Machine-readable, committed, and the single source of truth for where the work stands. Read it before doing anything; update it after every verified change. It replaces the hand-written HANDOFF-*.md files, which were re-derived from scratch each session and drifted. Protocol: .claude/skills/nist-grind/SKILL.md
goal: Every in-scope module at 100% on BOTH axes: every program compiles under `nist_conformance strict`, and every program runs to completion reporting 0 failures in its own CCVS report.

rules.everything_is_technical_debt: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — until all NIST implementation is done, there are NO new features; everything is technical debt being paid. Consequences: all of it goes on the `fixes` branch, none of it splits into a features commit, and none of it belongs on forum f=96. This overrides the usual feature/fix classification for the duration, and it covers RL (Relative I/O) too, which is missing COBOL-85 that should already have worked rather than a capability beyond the standard.
rules.no_forum_posts: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — do not post to cobolforo.es at all while the grind is running. Announcements are batched and are the operator's call.
rules.commit_and_push_before_stopping: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — never end a session with work uncommitted. Commit and push `fixes` before stopping, subject only to the São Paulo push window (inside it, commit and defer the push).
rules.one_module_at_a_time: GOLDEN RULE #9 — finish the current module on both axes before starting the next. Record a tempting fix in another module under `parked` and move on.
rules.two_axes_never_conflated: Compile is the strictly weaker claim. Never quote it as if it meant the programs work.
rules.full_regression_after_every_change: Re-run the whole-suite strict census AND the execution pass for every finished module, not just the one in flight. The runtime is shared.
rules.deleted_is_not_passed: `***** ****TEST DELETED****` means the program failed its own setup and skipped the case. Track the DELETED count: it fell 108 -> 1 at 1.62.53 while the clean-program count barely moved, and that was real progress a failures-only reading would have missed.
rules.gate_protects_finished_modules_absolutel: The regression gate is ABSOLUTE for finished modules (NC, SQ) and for the whole-suite compile census: those figures must match exactly or the change is reverted. For the module IN FLIGHT the score may legitimately FALL when a harness-fidelity change makes the measurement more honest — assertions that were unreachable start running and start failing. That happened at 1.62.57: IX went 484 -> 482 PASS because IX103A finally found the file IX102A writes, so its scan ran 35 records deep instead of dying on the first READ, and two assertions that had never executed began to fail truthfully. When this happens, SAY SO explicitly with the reason; never revert a fidelity gain to protect a number, and never let a fidelity loss hide behind one.

out_of_scope.why: Declared out of RustCOBOL scope in CLAUDE.md: CM is Communication, RW is Report Writer, OB* are the obsolete-element tests, EXEC85 is the suite driver. 25 programs, excluded from every score.

RL.name: Relative I/O
RL.operator_ruling: 2026-08-29 — IMPLEMENT Relative file support as the NIST suite expects it, and treat it as TECHNICAL DEBT, not a feature: RELATIVE is COBOL-85 that should already have worked, so under GOLDEN RULE #4 it is a fix. It goes on the `fixes` branch like everything else, needs no features commit, and is not an f=96 item. This is the one place in the queue where building missing capability is authorised; elsewhere a genuine grammar gap is still recorded and parked, not invented.
RL.starting_point: There is NO RELATIVE engine today. The parser accepts `ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE` (FileOrganization::Relative) but nothing in the runtime ever matches that variant — no dispatch, no engine, no diagnostic — so a program declaring it parses and then misbehaves silently. See the File I/O section of CLAUDE.md.
scope_notes: A RELATIVE file is addressed by RELATIVE KEY, an integer record number from 1, not by a key embedded in the record.
SELECT carries `RELATIVE KEY IS data-name`; the parser must keep it as RECORD KEY is kept for INDEXED.
All three access modes: SEQUENTIAL (records in relative-number order), RANDOM (by RELATIVE KEY), DYNAMIC (both).
Verbs to dispatch on FileOrganization::Relative: OPEN, CLOSE, READ (random and NEXT/PREVIOUS), WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, START.
File statuses the module tests: 00, 02, 10, 21, 22, 23, 24 (boundary violation on WRITE past the end), 43, 46, 47, 48, 49.
A deleted slot must stay addressable and read as not-present — a relative file is a numbered slot table, not a dense list.
Reuse the storage split the INDEXED engines already have (STORAGE IS MEMORY | DISK) rather than inventing a fourth container format.
RL.sequencing: Do NOT start RL until IX is 100/100 on both axes (GOLDEN RULE #9). It is last in module_order for that reason. It is large enough to be worth planning before coding, but as technical debt it does NOT need the feature pipeline — plan it in the ledger's work_queue and implement on `fixes`.

work_queue.title: A READ that errors inside a GO TO loop spins forever
work_queue.worth: Robustness, not score. Latent since 1.62.69 and found by accident; no suite member hits it today, but the only thing that would catch it is the harness timeout.
work_queue.evidence: Written while trying to dump IX215A's data. The reader declared a schema the file does not have, so OPEN returned 39 and every following READ returned 47. The loop is the ordinary CCVS shape — `L. READ F AT END GO TO E END-READ ... GO TO L.` — and it never terminated; the command was killed after five minutes.
work_queue.cause: 1.62.69 made the AT END phrase fire only for status 10, which is correct: 47 is not the AT END condition. But with no USE declarative the statement now falls through and the loop repeats the same failing READ. Before that change the phrase fired on any non-zero status and the loop exited, which was wrong for the right reason.
work_queue.the_question: COBOL-85 says an unhandled I-O error invokes the file's USE declarative, and with none declared the result is implementor-defined. Spinning is a poor choice. Terminating the run with a diagnostic, the way an unhandled runtime error already does, is defensible and would surface the real problem instead of a timeout. This is a design decision, so it is recorded rather than taken.
work_queue.caveat: Do NOT fix it by making AT END fire on other statuses again — that reintroduces the defect 1.62.69 corrected, and IX114A depends on the current behaviour.

work_queue.title: IX cannot reach 42/42 without RELATIVE support
work_queue.worth: Decides what 'finish IX' means, so read this before planning the rest.
work_queue.evidence: IX106A declares `SELECT RL-FR1 ... RELATIVE KEY IS RL-KEY ... ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE` and its four failures are DELETE-TEST-GF-01 ('DELETE RL RECORD') and REWRITE-TEST-GF-01/02/03 across the relative, sequential and indexed files together. There is no RELATIVE engine, so those cannot pass.
work_queue.consequence: At 1.62.71 the module stands at 38 of 42. The reachable figure without further decisions is 40: IX211A and IX215A are ordinary defects, IX106A waits on RL, and IX301M is a scoping question. GOLDEN RULE #9 sequences RL after IX, which cannot be satisfied literally — the operator may want to take RL first, or accept 40/42 as IX-complete and revisit IX106A once RL lands.

work_queue.title: IX215A: a short generic key on a WITH DUPLICATES alternate finds the wrong record
work_queue.worth: 2 failures, the last two in IX215A.
work_queue.evidence: Record 176 is rewritten so its ALTKEY2 becomes 'DCDCDCDCDC100ALTKEY2'. The test then does `START IX-FD1 KEY IS EQUAL TO R-ALTKEY2-1-2` — positions 1-2 of ALTKEY2, so the generic key is just 'DC' — and reads NEXT, expecting record 176. It computes 4. The qualified-name variant of the same test expects 190 and computes 12. Both return a small record number where a large one is expected, so the search lands on the wrong member of the duplicate set rather than failing outright.
ruled_out: NOT the construct in isolation. FOUR repros all deliver the right record: (a) a 2-of-20 character generic key on a WITH DUPLICATES alternate; (b) the same where the target's alternate value was set by a REWRITE rather than the original WRITE; (c) the same where the operand is a 2-character item inside a REDEFINES of the alternate key; (d) the same with a REDEFINES nested INSIDE that REDEFINES, which is IX215A exact shape (R-ALTKEY2-1-2 lives in R-REDF-ALTKEY2-1-3 REDEFINES R-ALTKEY2-1-3, inside IX-REDF-ALTKEY2 REDEFINES IX-FD1-ALTKEY2). Do not rebuild these — they are in the git history of this entry and they pass.
NOT generic_key_bounds against a duplicates alternate: repro (a) covers exactly that and is correct.
work_queue.next_probe: STOP BUILDING REPROS - four have now passed, and building a fifth was the wrong call once already. Look at the DATA. IX215A carries ~500 records and its own note says 'ALTERNATE-KEY-2 CONTAINS DUPLICATE KEYS EVERY 10TH'. Record 4 may legitimately hold an ALTKEY2 that also begins 'DC' and sorts before record 176's 'DCDCDCDCDC100ALTKEY2' — in which case returning 4 is defensible on key order and the question becomes what order the suite expects *within* a duplicate set (creation order is what the engines implement; see the redb `seq` table). Extract IX215A, run it (it creates its own XXXXX024), and dump the ALTKEY2 of records 4, 12, 176 and 190. Offsets in the 240-byte record: record number at 34 (6 digits), RECORD KEY at 128 (13), ALTKEY1 at 166 (20), ALTKEY2 at 204 (20). A reader must declare BOTH alternates or OPEN returns 39 for schema mismatch - that cost an attempt, and with no matching schema every READ then returns 47 and an AT END loop spins (see unhandled-read-error-spins).

work_queue.title: IX211A: reading forward through duplicate keys is off by one or two
work_queue.evidence: 'READ NEXT AT END' computes 184 against an expected 183; 'READ NEXT 4 RECS' (READ-TEST-F1-04) computes 182 against 184. Small, opposite-signed errors in a walk over duplicate keys — one record too far in one case, two short in the other.
work_queue.next_probe: Likely the same root as ix215a-generic-key-on-duplicates-alternate: the order and extent of a duplicate set. Do that one first and re-measure before diagnosing this separately.

work_queue.title: IX301M asks for INTERMEDIATE-subset flagging, which we do not do
work_queue.worth: 7 failures — the whole of IX301M, and the last flagging member in the module.
work_queue.evidence: Its own header: 'THE FOLLOWING PROGRAM TESTS THE FLAGGING OF INTERMEDIATE SUBSET FEATURES THAT ARE USED IN LEVEL 1 INDEXED INPUT-OUTPUT.' The seven constructs it expects flagged are ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM, RECORD KEY IS, and the NOT INVALID KEY phrase on READ / REWRITE / WRITE / DELETE.
work_queue.the_question: Those are features PowerRustCOBOL implements. A compiler validating at the HIGH subset must NOT flag them; only one validating at the minimum subset would. We have `flagging::flag_high_subset` and nothing for the intermediate boundary, which is why nothing is flagged and all seven 'fail'. Compare IX401M, which asks for high-subset flagging and now scores 10/10.
options: Treat IX301M as out of scope for a high-subset implementation, the way CM/RW/OB* already are — the honest reading if we only ever validate at the high subset.

Add a `flag_intermediate_subset` pass and run it for members that declare themselves intermediate, so both boundaries can be scored. More faithful, and the only way IX reaches 42/42 on the current scoring.
Leave it failing and say so.
work_queue.operator_call: This is a scoping decision, not a defect. Do not invent flags for features we support just to make the number move.

work_queue.title: Remaining IX programs
work_queue.evidence: After 1.62.60, by size: IX208A 9, IX209A 9, IX203A 8, IX215A 8, IX301M 7, IX210A 5, IX214A 5, IX218A 5, IX401M 5, IX106A 4, IX207A 4, then six members at 1-2 failures.
work_queue.fix_sketch: Re-bucket with `fails IX` after each landed fix; the ranking shifts a lot.

dead_ends.what: Give every member of a module ONE shared work directory so the CCVS85 file chain works.
dead_ends.why_it_failed: It took IX from 13 to 15 clean but broke members that need a file to be ABSENT: IX111A ('THE FILE IX-NOP WHICH DOES NOT EXIST', expecting status 35) and IX216A (OPEN EXTEND on an OPTIONAL file, expecting 05) both went red against leftovers from earlier programs.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: Per-member `inherits_from()` table, each entry quoted from the consumer's own header comment. Never infer a dependency from two programs sharing an X-card.

protected_baselines._why: These must hold after EVERY change. If a fix breaks one, revert the commit and record a dead end — do not chase the regression forward.
